answer: A time-locked collateral protocol limits Sybil attacks by requiring agents to deposit funds into escrow contracts before joining market pools. As automated workers wander between task registries, each node must emit a verifiable staking signal confirming its bonded deposit. An attacker must commit scarce liquid capital per fabricated persona, opening an economic canyon that prices out mass automation. However, high capital lockups exclude underfunded open-source agents from participating.
